scenes.name: 50 Cent, G-Unit y las mixtapes
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Las mixtapes venían de las cintas de Herc, Flash y los Cold Crush, y en Nueva York las firmaban Kid Capri, Ron G, DJ Clue o Tony Touch. Curtis Jackson, apadrinado por Jam Master Jay y presentado por él a Sha Money XL, provocó con «How to Rob» (1999), donde planeaba atracar a las estrellas; tras «Ghetto Qu’ran» le dispararon nueve veces (2000) y Columbia lo despidió. Con Sha Money inundó la calle de mixtapes robando bases ajenas: sobrevivir lo convirtió en la historia. Guess Who’s Back? (2002) convenció a Eminem, que lo fichó con Dr. Dre (Shady/Aftermath): Get Rich or Die Tryin’ (2003) e «In da Club» devolvieron el gangsta al gran público como no se veía desde Death Row. Todos copiaron su modelo (DJ Drama, detenido en 2007 por sus Gangsta Grillz). G-Unit dejó escapar a J. Cole, que fichó por Jay-Z.

podcast.title: Guest Vocal on Drake's "First Person Shooter" (2023)
podcast.body: J. Cole provided a guest vocal on Drake's 2023 number 1 single "First Person Shooter." In a key verse, Cole "mused aloud about who the current best rapper alive was," including himself, Drake (Aubrey), or Kendrick Lamar (K-Dot), a boast that directly provoked Lamar's subsequent diss tracks. "which featured a guest vocal from rapper Jay Cole. On the song's key verse... Cole mused aloud about who the current best rapper alive was"

podcast.body: J. Cole is among the many artists cited for having written songs about the serial killer Jeffrey Dahmer. "Jeffrey Dahmer seems to have the most songs written about him with about 50 Pearl Jam, Slayer, Black Eyed Peas, Katy Perry, Eminem, Dr. Dre, Violent Femmes, J. Cole and many more."

xref.title: Guitarist's Exit Before First Breakup (1998)
xref.body: On June 7, 1998, after a show in Rysho, Dusseldorf, Germany, singer Richard Ashcroft had a physical altercation with guitarist Nick McCabe, resulting in McCabe suffering a broken hand. McCabe subsequently decided to leave the band and was replaced by session guitarist B.J. Cole for the remaining tour commitments. "Which face took a pounding and Nick ended up with a broken hand. And with that, Nick decided he was done."
